name: application-grids
title: Grids
description: Column and row layout templates for arranging dashboard panels, cards, and content blocks in responsive multi-column grids.
useWhen: Arranging stat cards, chart panels, or content blocks side by side on medium and wide viewports.
Building a dashboard shell that adapts from single column on mobile to two or four columns on desktop.
Combining panels of different widths in the same row using span-based column assignments.
avoidWhen: Content order must change significantly between viewports — flexbox with reordering may be more appropriate.
Individual cells have complex content relationships — use a dedicated table component instead.
Only one column is ever needed — a simple stack of blocks does not require a grid wrapper.
responsiveBehavior: All grid variants collapse to a single column on small viewports and expand to their defined column count at md: and above.
accessibility: Grid containers are layout wrappers — use semantic elements inside cells (headings, articles, sections).
Reading order in the source matches the visual order so screen reader users navigate logically.
Do not use grid gaps or visual position alone to imply grouping — use semantic structure.

variants.title: 1x1
variants.description: Two equal-width columns side by side — the most common two-panel layout for dashboards.
accessibility: Column order in source must match intended reading order for screen reader users.

variants.title: 1x2
variants.description: A narrow left column and a wider double-width right column for a main-content-plus-sidebar arrangement.
accessibility: Ensure the narrower column is not a decorative sidebar that skips important context in source order.

variants.title: 2x1
variants.description: A wider double-width left column and a narrower right column for a main-content-plus-sidebar arrangement.
accessibility: Main content in the wider column should appear first in source order.

variants.title: 1x1x1
variants.description: Three equal-width columns for displaying three panels at the same visual weight.
accessibility: On narrow viewports, ensure column content stacks in a logical reading order.

variants.title: 1x1x1x1
variants.description: Four equal-width columns for stat cards or thumbnail grids on medium and large viewports.
accessibility: On mobile, the four-column grid collapses to a single column — verify content reads correctly.

variants.title: 1x1x2
variants.description: Three-column grid with two narrow cells and one double-width cell for highlighting a primary panel.
accessibility: The spanning column should not place critical content that breaks the source reading order.

variants.title: 2x1x1
variants.description: Three-column grid with a double-width leading cell and two narrower cells for a featured-plus-secondary layout.
accessibility: The featured cell appears first in source order, matching its visual prominence.

variants.title: 1x2x1
variants.description: Three-column grid with a wide center cell flanked by two narrower side panels.
accessibility: Left panel appears first in source; ensure screen reader users encounter panels in a logical order.

variants.title: Sidebar left
variants.description: A fixed-width left sidebar column beside a flexible main content area for application shell layouts.
accessibility: Sidebar navigation should come first in source order and be wrapped in a <nav> landmark.

variants.title: Sidebar right
variants.description: A flexible main content area beside a fixed-width right sidebar, for dashboards with supplementary info panels.
accessibility: Main content should appear before the sidebar in source order for optimal screen reader flow.
